matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the left‑hand side and right‑hand side (including any operators) to find the numeric difference.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: For "III = XV + XI", compute 3 vs 26, discrepancy = 23.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by adding or removing a single matchstick from each character in the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate possible one‑stick changes for each numeral/operator.
matchstick.example: I ↔ II, V ↔ X, X ↔ V, + ↔ –.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: Ensure that after removing a stick, the source character remains a valid Roman numeral or operator, and after adding the stick, the destination character also becomes a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For each candidate stick move generated in the enumeration step.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' yields '-', which is valid; adding that vertical to 'I' yields 'II', also valid.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: A diagonal stick from a V can be repositioned to cross the other diagonal, turning V (5) into X (10); conversely, removing a diagonal from X can create V, changing the value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy is a multiple of 5 and a V or X is present.
matchstick.example: Turning V into X adds 5 to the numeral’s value.

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical from II yields I (value –1). More generally, vertical sticks can be moved between I‑type characters to adjust values by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is 1 (or –1) and an I or II is present.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical to I in XI makes it XII, increasing the value by 1.

matchstick.title: Operator change – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical turns it into a minus sign, and adding a vertical to a minus creates a plus.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' or '–' and changing the operator could reduce the numeric discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '–' in "XV + XI" yields "XV – XI", decreasing the RHS by 22.

matchstick.title: Never alter the equality sign
matchstick.principle: The '=' sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; moving any stick away from it or adding to it invalidates the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process; any candidate move that touches the equality sign is discarded.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from '=' would break the sign, so such moves are prohibited.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical or horizontal stick, and vice versa.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick, ensure the orientation matches the target character’s required orientation.
matchstick.example: A diagonal from X cannot be placed on an I, because I requires a vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the entire equation to verify whether it now holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate transformation before committing to an answer.
matchstick.example: After moving the vertical from '+' to I, recompute RHS: XV – XII = 3, matching LHS.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus vertical transfer for numeral increment
matchstick.principle: If the equation is off by exactly one and a plus sign is present, you can move the vertical stick from the plus sign to an I, turning the plus into a minus and incrementing the I to II, adjusting the RHS by +1 and –22 simultaneously.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy equals 1 (or –1) and the equation contains a '+' and an I that can become II.
matchstick.example: In "III = XV + XI", moving the vertical from '+' to the I in XI yields "III = XV – XII", which balances.

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may ignore orientation constraints and assume any stick can become any other.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce the "Respect stick orientation" rule; only move sticks to positions that match the required orientation of the target character.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think any stick can be repurposed, overlooking the rule that the equality sign must stay unchanged.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the "Never alter the equality sign" rule; discard any move involving the '='.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: Removing a stick from a character such that the remaining shape is not a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Use the "Validate source and destination characters" rule to ensure both sides stay valid.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may treat operators as immutable.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the "Operator change – to + (or + to –)" skill whenever an operator is present.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may rely on visual plausibility rather than numeric correctness.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Follow the "Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move" step before finalizing the answer.
